claims.statement: The WMSC historical table names O’Brien as the 1991 champion; the extracted row reports seven competitors.
O’Brien reports leaving school at 16 and beginning memory training at 30 after a 1987 television demonstration.
The governing organisation places the first championship in London in 1991; its current rankings use a 2021 baseline.
O'Brien recalls a six-deck, zero-error world-record attempt in 1988, before the 1991 championship; no original adjudication record or exact date was located.

A secondary record table lists O'Brien's 35 inter-shuffled decks (1,820 cards, two errors) in 1990; the championship organiser retrospectively described him as a 35-deck Guinness holder before the October 1991 event.

The championship organiser's retrospective dates Memoriad '91 to 26 October 1991 and ranks O'Brien first among seven finishers; it separately names eight competitors and describes seven competition events, without documenting the entry pool or original scores.
Spinks’s round page dates her Bob Graham to 17–18 June 2005 and gives 23:33.
Her later account gives June 2005 and 23:32, one minute different from her round page.
Spinks recalls road running in 2001, then a Trunce advertisement while preparing for the Great North Run by October 2002.
The 2004 organiser’s table lists Nicky Spinks of Penistone eighth, 09:01:12, among 11 finishers and eight retired entries in Heart of Granite.
The 2024 account describes a first-female prize in 2004 while calling Spinks the only woman among 19 entrants. A category prize alone does not establish competitive selectivity.
Spinks reports route reconnaissance and a similar practice circuit from her farm; the dated interview does not quantify her early weekly hours.

Penistone Footpath Runners & AC lists Spinks among its 2005 Bob Graham Round completers and gives 23:33, supporting her round page over her later 23:32 account without supplying the original timing sheet.

In a 2022 England Athletics interview, Spinks recalled running on a farm in childhood and resuming recreational running at 19 while living in Manchester; she also recalled horse riding and cycling. These recollections do not establish competitive distinction.

A contemporary FRA table lists N. Spinks third woman, 50th of 69 finishers, at the Denis Stitt Memorial Race on 15 August 2002. The abbreviated name and unattached club leave attribution to Nicky probable rather than proven by this table alone.

A contemporary FRA table lists N. Spinks fourth woman, 43rd of 93 finishers, in the Trunce final race on 9 September 2002. Identity is abbreviated, and this placing is not a qualifying-result verdict.

The contemporary Trunce 1 table lists N. Spinks first of eight listed women and 83rd among 207 finishers on 31 March 2003. This is the earliest located category win, not yet the earliest qualifying excellence result.
The Hunshelf organiser explicitly names Nicky Spinks as first woman on 21 June 2003; its table lists N. Spinks 35th among 62 finishers and five women, 68:25.
The Broomhead Chase table lists N. Spinks first of three listed women, 22nd among 56 finishers, in 34:22 on 13 July 2003.

Spinks's 2017 challenge account calls 22 April 2017 her fiftieth birthday, and a sponsor's report two days later repeats it. The inferred birth date is 22 April 1967; both accounts ultimately depend on her report, not a birth record.
The author bibliography lists Starlight on 1 November 1983 and Heartsong on 28 February 1984.
Macomber calls Heartsong her first published book in 1982; that publication claim conflicts with her bibliography.
Macomber recalls selling articles, including one to Woman’s Day for $350, before the novel sale. No article title or acceptance date is supplied.
Macomber recalls rented equipment, household interruptions, studying four novels’ structures, and an editor’s rejection before another publisher bought the manuscript.
Publishers Weekly reports birth in 1948 and Starlight as the first novel in 1983. The year pair implies 34–35 at release, not an exact age or first-acceptance age.
LUP identifies Cleeves’s first published work as a chapter in its 1982 Hilbre volume, preceding her novel debut.
Cleeves recalls being asked by editor J. D. Craggs, a friend through bird-observatory connections, to contribute a human perspective. Commission and acceptance dates are absent.
Cleeves dates Hilbre residence to 1977–1981 and social-work study to the move; she describes diary writing and starting fiction during pregnancy leave.
Roberts and Andrews analyse A year on Hilbre and cite Cleeves’s 1982 chapter at pages 48–64; this independently corroborates attribution and publication, not acceptance timing.
Gyldendal's author biography gives Cleeves's birth year as 1954; a 1982 publication therefore falls at age 27–28, while an earlier chapter commission could still fall before 26.
ABC reports Goodwin as the 38-year-old winner on 19 July 2009, with judges George Calombaris, Gary Mehigan and Matt Preston. This dates reporting/broadcast, not filming.
The 2024 interview account reports elected Year 12 school captaincy at Hornsby Girls High School, an earlier selection needing its own threshold audit.
The same account describes interrupted education study, youth-group service, family IT work and creative cooking; it supplies no complete pre-26 achievement inventory.
Goodwin recalls a friend encouraging her application and time away from family and business during the show. Exact practice hours and pre-show paid cooking remain unknown.
The National Film and Sound Archive catalogues the 2009 MasterChef Australia finale, identifies Goodwin as winner and Poh Ling Yeow as runner-up, and credits producer Fremantle for the item.

A contemporaneous AAP report says the 2009 final scored Goodwin 82/100 and Poh Ling Yeow 75/100, and says 20 finalists were chosen from 7,500 applicants. Those are reported comparison pools, not the original casting or scoring records.
Jagani received the 2001 national second prize for Bullet-driven farm implements.
The award account dates a farmer-requested design to 1994 and an invited science-congress exhibition to January 2000; it does not date a built prototype or customer acceptance.
A later profile reports age 40, primary schooling, farm/diamond work, a year of welding training and a workshop operating for 22 years.
Contemporary reporting identifies Jagani demonstrating a bicycle spray pump in South Africa; the motorcycle tractor is attributed to Matukia.
Gujarati reporting describes changing a three-wheel Sanedo to four wheels after difficulties on uneven terrain; prototype and order dates are absent.
The first award account separates Jagani’s device from subsequent NIF/GIAN support and NID design assistance.
Mallesham is named national first in Mechanical and Electronics; the profile reports age 37.
The account dates development to 1992, the first machine made to 1999 and first sale to 2000; it reports childhood weaving and later electronics changes.
The interview reports age 43 in January 2018, inconsistent with age 37 in 2009.
The interview describes paid electrical work by day, development at night and family support; no practice-hour record is supplied.
Palle Srujana describes three years of development; the interview describes seven. Whether these refer to different phases is unknown.
The 2009 process used documentation, prior-art inquiry and advisory review of novelty and social utility; validation depth varied.
Jose is recorded as student first-prize recipient, reported age 17; the state booklet dates the award to 2005.
The contemporary June 2005 column reports age 17, earlier school-science prizes and construction at reported age 14.
The account attributes the initial diagram and instructions to Jose, material procurement to her father and fabrication to a workshop.
NIF records a patent application dated 7 August 2003; this is an application, not proof of a grant.
NDTV’s June 2006 caption places Class X work two years earlier, incompatible with treating that as the first construction date before the 2003 application.
The contemporary account connects the work to household responsibilities and records her then preference not to develop it further herself.
